name: Bandit / contextual-bandit & online RL serving features
category: New — online RL serving feature backend
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Bandit / contextual-bandit and online RL serving features — beava as the per-arm, per-(context, arm) and per-policy state backend that sits underneath a multi-armed-bandit (MAB), contextual-bandit (CMAB) or online-RL decision service, holding the rolling reward sufficient statistics (alpha, beta, n, sum_reward, sum_sq_reward), the per-(context, arm) interaction counters, the per-user exploration-exposure counters and the per-policy update tallies that the policy reads on every Rank/Decide call and writes on every Reward call.
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A bandit / online-RL decision service must, inside every Rank/Decide call (~5-30 ms end-to-end), read the up-to-date per-arm posterior parameters and per-(user, arm) interaction statistics for K arms and write the reward update atomically once an outcome arrives — so the next call sees the freshest possible state and the policy can shift traffic toward winning arms in seconds, not in the hourly retrain cycle of a batch model.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: Three concrete JTBDs distinguish this domain from items 18a (fraud classifier slice) and 18b (ranking slice). (1) Hold the per-arm sufficient statistics for a Thompson Sampling / Beta-Bernoulli MAB — alpha, beta, n_pulls, sum_reward, sum_sq_reward — keyed on (experiment_id, variant_id) or (campaign_id, creative_id), updated atomically on every reward event so the next sampling call sees the increment within milliseconds. This is the canonical 'where do we store the arm state so all serving instances agree' problem that Optimizely, LaunchDarkly, GrowthBook, Statsig, Eppo, AB Tasty, Convert, Kameleoon all solve internally and that the LinUCB / Online Matching / DoorDash-cuisine literature explicitly punts to Redis or Bigtable. (2) Hold the per-(context, arm) interaction features used inside a contextual bandit — rolling CTR, rolling conversion rate, rolling average reward, recency-decayed reward — keyed on the (user_segment, arm) or (context_bucket, arm) pair, plus the per-user exploration-exposure counters (how many times has this user been shown variant X in the last 24h, last 7d) that downstream cap / frequency / fatigue logic depends on. (3) Hold the per-policy update counters and policy-versioning metadata — number of updates since last full retrain, last update timestamp, number of arms currently live, per-arm last-pulled-at — that the online-RL controller reads to decide when to trigger a full LinUCB matrix inversion, a full Diag-LinUCB checkpoint, or a Vowpal-Wabbit policy reload. Beava covers (1) and (2) natively via @bv.table counters and per-entity atomic increments; (3) is straightforward to express as additional per-policy aggregations.
domain_fit.event_shapes: The bandit / online-RL vocabulary has three event families. (a) Decision events from the Rank/Decide API: decide {ts, request_id, user_id, experiment_id, arm_chosen, arm_set, context_features?, propensity?, policy_version} — typically one row per inbound request, used to update n_pulls and per-arm exposure counters. (b) Reward / outcome events: reward {ts, request_id, user_id, experiment_id, arm_id, reward_value, reward_type (click | conversion | dwell_ms | revenue | rating), latency_to_reward_ms} — delayed by anywhere from milliseconds (click) to hours (conversion) to days (subscription). (c) Policy / experiment lifecycle events: experiment_started, arm_added, arm_paused, policy_version_bumped, holdout_traffic_changed — low volume but state-changing for the bandit controller. Beava's @bv.event schemas map cleanly: decide is structurally identical to an impression event in 18b; reward is structurally identical to a delayed-conversion event in 3 (ad-tech) and 1a (CNP fraud) — the same delayed-attribution pattern that beava's existing demos already exercise.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Per-entity aggregations using beava @bv.table(key=...) primitives, organised by grain. ARM grain (key = (experiment_id, arm_id)) -> count(decide, total) = alpha+beta sufficient stat, count(reward where reward_value=1) = alpha, sum(reward_value, total) and sum_sq(reward_value, total) for Beta-Bernoulli posteriors and for Gaussian posteriors, distribution(reward_value, all) for T-Digest-style posterior summaries, velocity(decide, 1m / 1h), velocity(reward, 1m / 1h), rate(reward / decide, 1m / 1h / 24h) = rolling CTR / conversion rate, last_n(reward_value, n=1000) for non-stationary tracking. (USER, ARM) grain (key = (user_id, experiment_id, arm_id)) -> count(decide, 1h / 24h / 7d) = per-user exposure counter for frequency capping and exploration-fatigue, count(reward, 7d) for per-user per-arm reward history, time_since_last(decide), time_since_last(reward). (CONTEXT, ARM) compound grain (key = (context_bucket, experiment_id, arm_id), where context_bucket = a coarse user-segment / geo / time-of-day hash) -> rate(reward / decide, 1h / 24h) per segment-arm cell, used as the read-side feature for context-aware Thompson Sampling and as the warm-start prior for cold arms (DoorDash's regional-priors pattern). POLICY / EXPERIMENT grain (key = experiment_id) -> count(decide, total), count(reward, total), velocity(decide, 1m), n_unique(arm_id, total), last_update_at. Both exact (counters, sums) and approximate (HLL for distinct-user-exposure per arm, T-Digest for reward-distribution percentiles) primitives are useful; bandit-state correctness for the canonical TS / UCB algorithms requires exact counters at the arm grain.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Three parallel primary keys per decision: (experiment_id, arm_id) for the global per-arm posterior (K rows for K arms), (user_id, experiment_id, arm_id) for the per-user exposure / fatigue / personal-history features (K rows per active user per experiment), and (context_bucket, experiment_id, arm_id) for the per-segment per-arm conditional reward features (B * K rows where B is the number of coarse context buckets). Secondary grain: policy_version_id and request_id (for IPS / doubly-robust logging, but request_id is typically not aggregated server-side, only logged).
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Both unbounded ('lifetime of the experiment') and sliding (1m, 1h, 24h, 7d) windows are first-class. The unbounded counter is the textbook sufficient statistic for Thompson Sampling (alpha = total successes, beta = total failures over the life of the arm) — beava @bv.table counters with no window default to this shape. Sliding windows are essential for non-stationary bandits where reward distributions drift (seasonality, fashion, news cycles); the literature consistently warns that unbounded TS is brittle under non-stationarity and recommends 'discounted' or 'sliding-window' UCB / TS variants (the recency-decayed reward and the rolling-CTR features). Tumbling windows show up for offline-online consistency audits and for the 'compare arm A's last 24h to arm B's last 24h' dashboards. Approximate primitives (HLL for unique-user-exposure, T-Digest for reward percentiles) are tolerable at read time but the core (alpha, beta, n, sum_r) MUST be exact, because off-by-one errors in the posterior translate directly into biased traffic allocation. Session windows are rarely needed.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Idempotent-on-event-id is required, not strict exactly-once. Double-counting a reward event biases the posterior and the policy will over-exploit a falsely-strong arm; double-counting a decide event under-credits the arm's CTR and the policy will over-explore. Beava's atomic per-entity increments combined with an event_id dedupe key (or a (request_id, reward_type) dedupe key for rewards) cover this. The bandit literature treats double-counting as a worse problem than message loss, because loss is symmetric across arms while double-counting concentrates on whichever arm happened to retry — which is correlated with the chosen arm and therefore introduces a systematic bias. Distinct from item 18b (ranking) where double-counted clicks are harmless, and similar to item 14b (usage billing) and item 3 (ad cap) where strict idempotency is necessary.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Read latency budget per Rank/Decide call: 1-10 ms for the feature fetch sub-budget, inside a 20-100 ms end-to-end Rank API budget. Microsoft Personalizer used Vowpal Wabbit specifically for 'maximum throughput and lowest latency' on Rank/Reward calls; Optimizely Agent 4.3 (Nov 2025) caches CMAB decisions in an LRU + Redis to hold the round-trip under tens of ms; Netflix's artwork-personalization pre-computes the bandit decision into EVCache and serves images at >20M requests/sec; DoorDash cuisine bandits run inside the explore-page render path. Beava's published sub-millisecond TCP get / batch_get sits comfortably inside this envelope for the typical K=2-200 arm * 1-user * ~5-feature shape per Rank call. Reward writes have a softer budget (the policy can absorb 10s of ms of write latency without hurting the next decision) but still want to be sub-10 ms p99 because every reward becomes a write amplification across the (user, arm) and (context, arm) compound keys.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Seconds, often sub-second. The whole point of a bandit over a static A/B test is that arm allocations adapt within seconds of seeing a reward — Statsig describes Autotune as 'continuously adjusting traffic'; LaunchDarkly MAB 'continuously evaluates variation performance and automatically shifts traffic'; the Online Matching / Diag-LinUCB paper explicitly motivates a 'real-time bandit system' against the staleness of batch retraining. Spotify's neural CMAB on the Home page (March 2025) and Apple's Two-Layer Bandit (ICML 2025) both emphasise rapid posterior updates. Beava's push-on-event architecture delivers single-digit-ms feature staleness for the reward to next-decision loop, which exceeds the SLA — the freshness becomes 'whatever the upstream attribution pipeline produces' rather than 'whatever the feature-store batch cadence allows'.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Mixed, with steady-state determined by Rank-API traffic. Public references span four orders of magnitude. Netflix artwork: >20M personalized image requests/sec at peak (although these are pre-computed from the bandit, not live bandit calls). YouTube Online Matching: serves billions of users and millions of items via Diag-LinUCB on Bigtable. DoorDash cuisine filter: full DoorDash mobile-app traffic. LaunchDarkly / Optimizely / Statsig CMAB on an enterprise customer: 1k-100k Rank calls/sec depending on the surface. Mid-market experimentation platform (GrowthBook / Eppo / AB Tasty / Convert / Kameleoon enterprise tier): 100-10k Rank calls/sec per customer. Each Rank call produces 1 decide event (write) and ~K arm-state reads (where K = 2-200 for most production bandits); each Reward call produces O(K) writes after fan-out to (user, arm) and (context, arm) compound keys. Steady-state for a mid-size bandit deployment is therefore comfortably inside beava's published 684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack+parallel=16). [uncertain] no public benchmark of beava-shaped batch_get over (1 user * K arms * ~5 features) at K=100.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Read-heavy by a factor of K (number of arms). One decide call reads K arm rows (and optionally K (user, arm) rows and K (context, arm) rows), then writes 1 decide row; one reward call writes O(K) rows after the fan-out across grains. For K=10 arms and a 50:1 decide:reward ratio (typical when reward is conversion-rate, ~2%), the read:write ratio is roughly 10:1 to 30:1. This is closer to the ranking shape (18b) than to the fraud shape (1a-1c), but with much smaller fan-out (K ~ 10s, not 100s of candidates).
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Tractable. Per-(experiment_id, arm_id) row at maybe 200-500 bytes (alpha, beta, n, sum_r, sum_sq_r, last_pulled_at, T-Digest of reward, last_n reward values) * K arms * E concurrent experiments. For an experimentation platform running 1,000 concurrent bandit experiments with average K=10 arms = 10K rows of arm-grain state = ~5 MB. The (user, arm) compound grain is the cardinality risk: MAU * K_active * ~50 bytes. For 10M MAU with on average 3 active bandit experiments each having K=5 arms = 150M rows * 50 bytes = ~7.5 GB. For 100M MAU at the same shape = 75 GB, which fits on a single beava box. The (context, arm) compound grain is naturally bounded (B context buckets * K * E) and small. Total typical state size is 10-100 GB, well inside beava's in-memory ceiling for mid-market deployments and at the edge for hyperscale (Netflix / YouTube / TikTok / Spotify-class) bandits.
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Bounded on the arm and experiment axes (K is usually 2-200, E is usually 10-10,000 across a platform), slowly-growing on the user axis (MAU), bounded on the context-bucket axis (deliberate coarsening to keep the (context, arm) grain tractable). The (user, arm) compound grain is the explosive axis if not capped; bandit deployments routinely TTL per-user arm-history after 7-30 days to keep it manageable. Cardinality is fundamentally LOWER than ranking (18b), where item_id is unbounded; that makes the bandit-state slice an easier fit for beava's single-binary in-memory model than full ranking is.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Mixed. Per-arm posterior state lives the lifetime of the experiment (days for short campaign tests, months for ongoing personalization bandits, indefinite for always-on always-learning policies like Spotify Home content-type calibration). Per-(user, arm) history typically TTLs at 7-30 days for fatigue / frequency-cap features, and may live for the experiment lifetime for long-horizon personalization. Per-(context, arm) prior state persists for the lifetime of the segmentation taxonomy (months to years). Logged decide/reward events for off-policy evaluation live for years in the warehouse, NOT in beava.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: Per Rank call: typically K * ~5-15 per-arm features (alpha, beta, n, rolling CTR, recency-decayed reward, sum_r, sum_sq_r, T-Digest percentile, last-pulled-at) + 1 * ~5 user-side context features (geo bucket, device, hour-of-day, day-of-week, segment_id) + optionally K * ~3-5 (user, arm) features (exposure counter, time-since-last-exposure, per-user per-arm CTR) + optionally K * ~3-5 (context, arm) features (segment-conditional CTR, segment-conditional reward) + ~5 policy-level features (policy_version, last_update_at, num_updates_since_retrain). For K=10 arms this is roughly 50-200 features per Rank call — a clean fit for a single batch_get and squarely in the 'beava sweet spot' shape of one batched call returning a dense vector.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Best-effort to crash-safe is sufficient for the online posterior; the long-term durable copy lives in the off-policy log in the warehouse. Recovering 10-60 seconds of recent reward updates after a crash is acceptable because (a) the upstream event bus replays them on restart, (b) the policy is robust to small posterior perturbations, and (c) the alternative is to add WAL latency to every reward write, which directly inflates the freshness metric the buyer is selecting beava FOR. Regulator-grade durability is NOT required, distinct from item 8 (AML), 14b (billing) and parts of 1a (CNP fraud). The interesting durability nuance is that bandit state must survive a single-node restart without corruption — a half-written alpha leads to silent bias — and beava's WAL + snapshot semantics cover that with margin.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary regional fits a single-region experimentation platform, an in-house bandit deployment at a startup-to-mid-market SaaS, an edge-deployed bandit for a single product surface. The natural deployment is one beava per region per environment (staging / prod), co-located with the bandit / online-RL decision service. Multi-region active-active for a global experimentation platform (Optimizely / LaunchDarkly / Statsig at global scale) is NOT supported in beava v0 — the per-arm posterior is the single source of truth and must converge across regions, which beava cannot do natively. The Diag-LinUCB / Online Matching pattern (offline-aggregate + online-apply) sidesteps this for hyperscale and is the documented workaround for v0.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Primary buyer: the ML platform / experimentation-platform team — at experimentation vendors (Optimizely, LaunchDarkly, Eppo / Datadog, Statsig, GrowthBook, AB Tasty, Convert, Kameleoon) building MAB / CMAB features into their products, and at in-house ML platform teams (Spotify, Netflix, DoorDash, Instacart, Pinterest, ByteDance / TikTok, Meta / Instagram, Roblox, Wayfair, Apple) building bandit / online-RL services in production. Secondary buyer: the growth / personalization / lifecycle-marketing team that wants a turn-key bandit-as-a-feature inside an email-send or push-notification orchestrator (Braze CTA bandits, Hightouch AI Decisioning, Amplitude Experiment MAB). Tertiary buyer: ad-tech yield-management teams running multi-armed bidding bandits for creative selection, publisher selection, or RTB bid-shading (overlaps with item 3 buyers).
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large and growing, well-documented in 2025 transactions. Datadog acquired Eppo for $220M in May 2025 explicitly to expand into 'AI, product analytics, experimentation and feature flag capabilities' — the single largest public marker for the experimentation-platform TAM. Statsig processes >1 trillion events/day for customers including OpenAI, Figma, Notion, Atlassian, Flipkart, Brex. Eppo's annual contracts ranged $15k-$87k pre-acquisition (median $42k). Optimizely Agent 4.3 (Nov 2025) and 4.4 added production CMAB. LaunchDarkly, GrowthBook, AB Tasty, Convert, Kameleoon, Amplitude Experiment all shipped MAB / CMAB features in 2024-2025. Netflix, Spotify, DoorDash, YouTube (Online Matching paper, 2023), Apple (Two-Layer Bandit ICML 2025), Wayfair (WayLift, contextual bandits for paid media) all publish bandit production case studies. Microsoft Personalizer (Azure Cognitive Service, retiring Oct 2026) was the named 'first real-world reinforcement-learning service'. AB testing software market is projected at substantial double-digit-billion scale by 2030 (Future Market Insights); the bandit-state slice is a small but central layer in this stack. [uncertain] precise dollar TAM for the 'bandit-state backend' slice itself — vendors do not break it out.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: Three forces. (1) Datadog's Eppo acquisition (May 2025) plus Optimizely Agent 4.3 (Nov 2025) production CMAB plus Spotify's deployed Home-page CMAB (March 2025) make 2025 the year experimentation went from 'A/B test result tables' to 'live adaptive policy' for enterprise buyers — the buyer's competition just shipped a bandit, so they ship one too. (2) Generative-AI product surfaces (LLM-powered chat assistants, AI-generated content, prompt-bandit selection) need rapid online adaptation that batch experiments cannot deliver — the new wave of 'AI Decisioning' (Hightouch, Braze AI Decisioning, AB Tasty Evi Nov 2025) is bandit infrastructure with an LLM front-end. (3) The 'Vowpal-Wabbit + Redis' or 'in-house TS on Redis with Lua scripts' DIY stack that powered the first generation of production bandits (Yahoo news LinUCB, Microsoft Personalizer, Saavn, DoorDash, Udemy MAB tutorial series, Tata Digital uncertainty-aware bandits) is now visibly under-engineered for the multi-experiment, multi-tenant, sub-second-freshness workload that modern platforms demand — and Microsoft's announcement that Personalizer retires October 2026 leaves a concrete gap that needs to be filled.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: Light relative to fraud (1a-1c), AML (8), KYC (9), billing (14b). GDPR / CCPA apply at the per-user grain — right-to-erasure requires per-user delete that propagates through the (user, arm) state. EU DSA / DMA ranking-transparency obligations attach to very large platforms running bandits over content / amplification, but the obligation is documentation, not state storage. The new EU AI Act creates 'high-risk' classifications for some personalization use cases (credit, employment, public services) and bandit policies that adapt continuously will need policy-version logging and replay capability — that's an OFF-LINE log obligation, not an online-state one, but it shapes the audit story. SOC 2 Type II is table stakes for the platform that hosts the bandit. No PCI / FFIEC / HIPAA exposure in typical deployments.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: A runnable Beta-Bernoulli Thompson-Sampling MAB on top of beava with @bv.event for decide / reward and @bv.table for per-arm alpha / beta is roughly a 1-day demo — the primitives all exist, the schema is two events and three counters, and the policy is ~50 lines of Python that samples from Beta(alpha+1, beta+1) on every Rank call. A realistic CMAB with per-(context, arm) buckets, per-user exposure caps and warm-start priors is a 1-2 week effort. A full Vowpal-Wabbit-class LinUCB replacement integrated with beava-held state is a multi-quarter project because matrix inversion and policy retraining live OUTSIDE beava. This positions item 24 as a high-leverage wedge: an experimentation vendor can pilot beava as their MAB-state backend in a week, and a Microsoft-Personalizer-replacement community demo could be a several-day project once Personalizer retires in October 2026.

competition.incumbents: Three layers. (a) Bandit-state inside production experimentation platforms: Optimizely (production CMAB in Agent 4.3 Nov 2025, in-memory LRU + Redis for shared decision caching), LaunchDarkly (Thompson Sampling MAB, multiple MABs per flag), GrowthBook 3.3 (bandits in beta), Statsig (Autotune MAB at trillion-events/day scale), Eppo / Datadog (warehouse-native + SDK CMAB), AB Tasty (dynamic allocation MAB), Convert (Multi-Arm Bandit in higher tiers), Kameleoon (MAB optimization for feature experiments), Amplitude Experiment (MAB GA), Dynamic Yield (CMAB optimization), Braze (MAB for messaging CTAs and AI Decisioning), Hightouch (MAB in AI Decisioning). (b) Bandit-state inside in-house ML platforms: Microsoft Personalizer (Vowpal-Wabbit-backed, retiring Oct 2026), Vowpal Wabbit + Redis (the canonical OSS reference), Amazon SageMaker RL (Vowpal-Wabbit-on-SageMaker for production CB), TensorFlow Agents (LinUCB / Neural-LinUCB with per-arm features), Seldon Core thompson-sampling router (Redis state persistence), Saavn / JioSaavn (in-house CB for personalization), DoorDash (in-house TS with regional warm-start), YouTube Online Matching (Diag-LinUCB on Bigtable for billions of users / millions of items), Netflix artwork-personalization (EVCache-backed pre-computed bandit), Spotify Home neural CMAB (March 2025), Apple Two-Layer Bandit (ICML 2025), Wayfair WayLift CB for paid media, Tata Digital uncertainty-aware bandits. (c) Online KV / streaming substrates used to BUILD the bandit-state backend: Redis / Redis Enterprise / ElastiCache (the canonical default), Bigtable (Online Matching), DynamoDB, EVCache (Netflix), Aerospike, Apache Flink + Kafka (the Confluent / Kai Waehner real-time-feature-store pattern), Spark Structured Streaming.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific bandit-product vendors that buyers might procure as a black box: Microsoft Personalizer (retiring Oct 2026 — a gap), Amazon Personalize (managed personalization with bandit + deep models), Dynamic Yield (CMAB-based personalization), Persado (generative + bandit for marketing copy), Optimizely Personalization, Adobe Target. These compete with the buyer's in-house bandit-decision service, not directly with beava; beava is the state layer underneath whichever decision engine the buyer uses. Closest direct competitor in the state-backend role is Redis (in any of its flavours) with Lua scripts for atomic posterior updates — Optimizely Agent and Seldon Core both explicitly document Redis as the multi-instance bandit-state store.
competition.beava_differentiator: Seven concrete differentiators for the bandit / online-RL slice. (1) Atomic per-arm increment primitives — alpha += 1, beta += 1, n_pulls += 1, sum_reward += r — are exactly what beava's @bv.table counters already provide, with single-RTT push on every reward event; Redis offers INCRBY but you build the (request_id, arm_id, event_id) dedupe in Lua, while beava ships event-id idempotency natively. (2) Compound-key support (user_id, experiment_id, arm_id) and (context_bucket, experiment_id, arm_id) natively, with no client-side key construction or Lua glue. (3) The 50+ aggregation primitives include exactly the rolling-CTR / recency-decayed-reward / last-N / velocity shapes the contextual-bandit literature wants — DoorDash's regional-prior pattern is one (geo, cuisine) compound key + a sliding rate primitive. (4) Push-on-event over HTTP/JSON :8080 and framed TCP / msgpack :8081 maps cleanly to the Rank/Reward API shape; the Microsoft Personalizer Rank to EventHub to Reward loop is structurally identical to the beava push-event loop. (5) Apache-2.0, single binary, no Kafka required — a small experimentation-platform team can stand up the bandit-state layer without standing up Flink + Kafka + Redis (the canonical 2025 stack documented in the Confluent / Kai Waehner online-feature-store blog and the Jaehyeon Kim event-driven-recommender series). (6) batch_get for K arms * M features in a single TCP round trip is the natural shape of a Rank API and is exactly the I/O pattern that drives Optimizely Agent's CMAB decision cache. (7) The Personalizer retirement (Oct 2026) opens a documented hole — a 'self-hosted Personalizer replacement built on beava + Vowpal Wabbit' is a high-relevance positioning for late-2025 / 2026.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: Eight concrete gaps that block production bandit deployments today. (1) No TLS / no auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 — an experimentation vendor cannot put beava in a customer VPC without at least bearer-token auth and ideally mTLS. Hard blocker for SaaS procurement. (2) No multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs — a hosted-MAB SaaS cannot safely host multiple customers' arm-state on one box; the experimentation-platform buyer (Statsig / Eppo / Optimizely) needs per-tenant isolation. (3) No in-process sharding — Netflix / YouTube / TikTok / Spotify-class bandit state spans multiple TB in some configurations and exceeds a single beava box; the Diag-LinUCB / Online Matching pattern works around this but only by moving the heavy parameter aggregation OUTSIDE beava onto Bigtable. (4) No native vector / matrix primitive — full LinUCB needs a per-arm A-matrix (d * d) and b-vector; beava can store the flattened matrix as a fixed-size bytes value but does not offer the atomic outer-product update primitive that Lua-on-Redis or Bigtable column-family updates provide. This pushes full LinUCB outside beava's sweet spot and back into 'beava holds counters, an external service holds matrices'. (5) No triggers — useful for 'fire when arm n_pulls < threshold and elapsed > T to escalate exploration' or 'fire when policy_version != current to reload the served model'. (6) No published batch_get benchmark for the (1 user * K=100 arms * ~10 features) Rank-shape — the 684k EPS headline is the WRITE-side number, not the read shape. (7) No off-policy / IPS logging primitive — bandit deployments require logging (context, action, propensity, reward) tuples for off-policy evaluation; beava can store the counters but the logged-tuple log itself lives in Kafka or the warehouse and beava does not currently document that integration. (8) No cross-region replication for global multi-region bandits where arm posteriors must converge across regions.
competition.integration_surface: Upstream producers in item 24: HTTP webhooks from the Rank/Decide service (sending decide events as fast as decisions are made), HTTP webhooks from the Reward attribution service (often delayed, often joined inside Flink or Spark Structured Streaming before pushing the joined reward to beava), mobile-SDK direct push for in-app clicks / dwell / conversion that are attributable on the device, Kafka / Kinesis for buyers who already run a streaming bus and want to fan the bandit feedback through it (the Confluent Apache-Kafka-and-Flink online-feature-store blog from Sept 2025 is the canonical reference). Downstream consumers are the bandit decision service (Vowpal Wabbit, LinUCB, Neural-LinUCB on TF-Agents, custom Thompson-Sampling Python, Spotify-style neural CMAB, Apple Two-Layer Bandit) pulling features via batch_get on every Rank call, plus the offline off-policy-evaluation pipeline pulling the logged decide/reward tuples from the durable log (NOT from beava). Beava sits between the event producer and the decision service, exposing posterior state via batch_get and accepting reward updates via push.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Rules / policy engine: simple Beta-Bernoulli TS or epsilon-greedy is ~50 lines of policy code outside beava (the Seldon Core thompson-sampling router pattern), pulling alpha/beta from beava and emitting an arm choice. ML scorer: contextual bandit / online RL stacks (Vowpal Wabbit, LinUCB, Diag-LinUCB, Neural-LinUCB, two-layer hierarchical bandits per Apple's ICML 2025 paper, Spotify's neural CMAB) treat beava as a fast feature backend (per-(context, arm) rolling CTR, per-user exposure counters, per-arm sufficient statistics) and run the model in-process or as a side car. The contract is the same as in item 18b: batch_get(entity_ids, feature_names) -> dense vector, plus push(event) -> atomic state update.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No publicly named beava users running this use case yet. adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: Mostly passive load, with one notable exception. The core feedback loop (decide -> reward -> posterior update) has no active adversary trying to corrupt the state. However, in two adjacent settings — affiliate-marketing bandits and ad-creative-selection bandits — there IS adversarial pressure to inflate the reward of a specific arm (click farms, bot conversions, motivated insiders). That adversarial pressure is handled by upstream click-fraud / ad-fraud filtering (item 3) before the reward reaches the bandit-state backend, and is NOT a beava-side problem. Feature drift in this domain is driven by genuine non-stationarity (seasonality, fashion, exogenous shocks) rather than by an adversary.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: Beava is the wrong tool for: (1) Off-policy evaluation of historical bandit logs — that requires the full (context, action, propensity, reward) tuple log replayed against counterfactual policies, which belongs in a warehouse / batch system, not in an in-memory online state backend. (2) Storing the LinUCB A-matrix (d * d, with atomic outer-product updates) at d > ~50 — beava counters can hold the bytes but the atomic matrix-update primitive is not first-class; Bigtable or Redis-Lua are better at d > 50. (3) Cross-region active-active bandit posterior convergence for global experimentation platforms — v0 has no replication. (4) Multi-tenant SaaS bandit-state hosting where each customer's state must be isolated — no namespace ACLs in v0. (5) Long-horizon RL (PPO / Q-learning / actor-critic) where the trajectory is dozens-to-thousands of steps and the state is high-dimensional — beava primitives are scalar counters, not trajectory replay buffers. The contextual-bandit / Personalizer-style one-step RL is in scope; full multi-step RL is not. (6) The Rank-API decision LOGIC itself — beava is the state layer, not the policy engine. (7) Model storage (Vowpal Wabbit weights, neural-CMAB checkpoints) — those live in a model registry / object store.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship for the bandit / online-RL slice, in rough priority order. (1) TLS + bearer-token / mTLS auth on :8080/:8081 — hard blocker for any experimentation-vendor or enterprise-ML-platform buyer to put beava in a customer / corporate VPC. (2) Multi-tenancy / namespace ACLs — hard blocker for hosted-MAB SaaS where each customer is a separate tenant of the same beava deployment. (3) Published p99 batch_get benchmark for the (1 user * K=10..200 arms * ~10 features) Rank shape, with a crates/beava-bench/configs/bandit-rank.json workload definition; target p99 < 2 ms feature-fetch under sustained 10k Rank/s. (4) Native event-id idempotency on the push path for reward events — beava already has atomic counters but the (request_id, arm_id, event_id) dedupe key handling needs to be a documented first-class primitive, not a user-side concern, because double-counting biases the posterior in a way the buyer cannot tolerate. (5) python/beava/demos/bandit/ — a runnable Beta-Bernoulli Thompson-Sampling MAB on @bv.table counters, plus a contextual-bandit demo with per-(context, arm) buckets and per-user exposure caps, plus a 'Microsoft-Personalizer-replacement' demo combining beava + Vowpal Wabbit. This is the single highest-leverage artefact to ship before October 2026 (Personalizer retirement). (6) Right-to-erasure helper that propagates a per-user delete through the (user, experiment_id, arm_id) compound grain — GDPR / CCPA compliance. (7) Triggers — 'fire when policy_version mismatch' to reload the bandit policy, 'fire when arm under-explored' to escalate exploration. (8) Documented sidecar pattern for an off-policy log (Kafka topic for the (context, action, propensity, reward) tuples that an offline OPE pipeline consumes). (9) Optional helper for matrix-update primitives (atomic outer-product on a per-arm fixed-size byte blob) — only needed if beava wants to handle full LinUCB inside the box; otherwise document the 'beava holds counters, external service holds matrices' split. (10) Cross-region replication for global multi-region bandit deployments (post-v1, large effort). (11) Per-arm TTL / per-(user, arm) TTL for fatigue / frequency-cap features — partially covered by beava's per-entity TTL story but needs documentation for this domain. (12) Per-tenant quota / rate-limiting on :8080/:8081 for multi-customer SaaS deployments.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Optional but high-value. Pure feature serving (read posterior, write reward) is sufficient for the canonical TS / UCB / LinUCB loop. Triggers would unlock: 'fire when arm n_pulls below floor and elapsed > T' for cold-arm exploration boost, 'fire when policy_version != current' for hot policy reload, 'fire when sum_reward / n_pulls diverges from prior by > threshold' for non-stationarity detection, 'fire when per-user exposure_count crosses cap' for frequency-cap enforcement. None of these is a hard blocker because the bandit decision service can poll on every Rank call, but trigger-based eventing reduces wasted reads and supports the 'sub-second adaptive policy' positioning that distinguishes bandits from static A/B tests.
